documents.html:
(Celetel × CelChat) × Limedock

GTM Autopilot: Scope of Work & Service Agreement for fully automated go-to-market, lead generation and customer acquisition
Prepared for Lalit, Founder — Celetel (incl. CelChat)
Prepared by Ranjeet Ratan — Limedock
Date 4 November 2026
Version 1.0
Fee ₹30,000 per month (subscription), with a 50% advance (₹15,000) on approval
Valid until 4 December 2026

1. The one-line summary

We build and run an automated growth machine for Celetel and CelChat. It finds your ideal customers, reaches them on every channel, warms them up, books demos, converts trials into paid accounts, and reports everything to you daily on Telegram (or WhatsApp). You see the reports. We run the machine.

The end goal is not likes or followers. It is qualified leads → demos → paying customers → revenue. Every workflow in this document exists to move one of those numbers.

We connect everything in Week 1, have every core automation running by the end of Week 3, then optimise and repeat every week until we find the repeatable path from lead to paying customer (see Section 4).

2. Our understanding of your business
Company Celetel (CelChat is its product unit)
Headquarters A-111, Sector 63, Noida, Uttar Pradesh 201301, India (as listed on Celetel's LinkedIn page)
Founder Lalit (linkedin.com/in/lalit01)
LinkedIn linkedin.com/company/celetelasia (1,224 followers)

2.1 Brand architecture

Celetel (parent) CelChat (product unit)
What it is Enterprise CPaaS: WhatsApp Business API, RCS, SMS (DLT), Voice, AI Agents, bulk campaigns, workflow builder Omnichannel conversation workspace: one inbox for WhatsApp, Instagram DMs, RCS, WebChat and Gmail, with routing, SLAs, notes and analytics
Revenue model Subscription (₹1,599 – ₹5,999/mo + Enterprise) plus usage (per message) Seat and workspace subscription (14-day trial), channel costs billed separately
Primary buyer Founders, CMOs, growth and CRM heads, CTOs and product heads (OTP and notifications) Heads of Customer Support/CX, contact-centre managers, D2C ops leads
Market India-first (DLT, INR pricing), international routes to 100+ countries Global-ready (CelChat Inc., BYO provider: Twilio, Vonage, Infobip, Bird)
Key proof Official Meta Tech Partner, SOC 2 / ISO 27001 / GDPR claims, transparent pricing 500+ organisations, 12k+ active agents, 98M+ messages sent
Verticals E-commerce, BFSI, Healthcare, Logistics, Real Estate, Hospitality, EdTech, Travel, Automotive, OTT, SaaS, FMCG/D2C E-commerce, BFSI, Healthcare, Education, Travel & Hospitality, Real Estate

How we will run them: two distinct funnels (different buyers, different messages) on one shared data and automation layer, with built-in cross-sell:

  • Every Celetel customer is a CelChat prospect ("you send on Celetel; now manage every reply in one inbox").
  • Every CelChat customer using another provider is a Celetel prospect ("switch your India traffic to Celetel and pay less per message").

2.2 Optional idea (only if you approve): grow Celetel using Celetel

Everything in this scope runs on our own stack and does not need your platform. As a simple optional idea: if you approve, we can also run parts of the GTM on your own products. For example, WhatsApp follow-ups could go out through Celetel, DMs and website chats could be handled in CelChat, and demo reminders could be sent over RCS or SMS.

The benefit is that your own growth engine becomes a live case study ("how Celetel grows using Celetel"). This is entirely your call. Nothing in this agreement depends on it, and we will only do it if you say yes.

3. What we found: current-state audit snapshot

From a review of celetel.com, celchat.com and public profiles (4 Nov 2026). Everything below is fixable in the first 2–3 weeks. These are the quick wins.

Strengths to build on

  • Transparent public pricing. This is rare among Indian CPaaS players and a strong conversion lever.
  • Meta Tech Partner status plus 12 industry solution pages with ready-made flows.
  • Free trial with no credit card on both brands, so the product-led motion is already possible.
  • The contact form already captures service interest and monthly message volume. That is lead-scoring data we can use from day one.
  • An active LinkedIn page (1,224 followers) posting several times a week on strong, useful topics: COD confirmation, OTP fallback, TRAI DLT compliance and healthcare messaging.
  • CelChat's "bring your own provider" connectors (Twilio, Vonage, Infobip, Bird) are a wedge into global accounts that already pay another CPaaS.

Gaps to close

# Finding Why it matters
1 No Google Analytics 4, Google Tag Manager, Meta Pixel or LinkedIn Insight Tag detected on the pages we checked (CelChat only runs Cloudflare Web Analytics). To be confirmed in the kickoff audit. No attribution, no retargeting, and ads cannot optimise for leads. Today you cannot see which channel produces paying customers.
2 No social media links on either website. Celetel's LinkedIn page (linkedin.com/company/celetelasia) and other social profiles are not linked from celetel.com or celchat.com. Visitors can't find or follow your social proof from the website, and your social channels get no traffic from it.
3 Search name collision with similarly named Indian CPaaS players (e.g. Celitix) and Celcom brands. Branded search traffic leaks to competitors. Needs a brand-defence SEO and ads plan.
4 CelChat.com is a client-side-rendered app. Crawlers that don't execute JavaScript see only the page title. Weak organic indexing and near-invisibility to AI answer engines (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini), where many B2B software searches now start.
5 No blog, resources, case studies or named testimonials on celetel.com (CelChat has one testimonial). No organic acquisition engine, and BFSI and enterprise buyers need proof before booking a demo.
6 Proof numbers disagree across pages: "5,000+ businesses / 10M+ messages a day" (home) vs "300+ active clients / 120M+ messages daily" (About). The pricing copy says both "free plan" and "14-day trial". Inconsistent claims hurt credibility, especially with enterprise procurement. Must be aligned before we spend on ads.
7 Basic SEO hygiene: duplicate title ("About Us - Celetel | Celetel") and generic meta descriptions ("telecommunications solutions and services"). Lower click-through from search results.
8 Low LinkedIn engagement: recent posts get about 1–6 reactions each on 1,224 followers. The About section is abstract and doesn't say clearly what you sell or who it's for, CelChat isn't mentioned, and CTAs aren't tracked. Good content isn't reaching buyers. Founder-led posting, employee amplification, better formats and tracked CTAs fix this.

4. How we work: connect fast, then optimise and repeat

4.1 Fast setup, careful scaling

  • Week 1: connect everything. Accounts, tracking, CRM, Claude Code, Grok bots and mailboxes, lead sources (ICP databases, Product Hunt, Google Maps), WhatsApp Business numbers and the daily report.
  • Weeks 2–3: switch the automations on. By the end of Week 3, every core automation is running.
  • Week 4 onward: optimise and repeat. Every week we measure, keep what works, fix or switch off what doesn't, and scale the winners.

Every automation still starts on a small batch and is scaled only once the numbers look healthy. This protects Celetel's brand, its email domains and its WhatsApp numbers.

4.2 Setup time: 3 weeks

Everything is connected within 1 week, and all core automations are running within 3 weeks. The first leads from cold email are expected in Week 2, and volume grows as each automation comes online.

4.3 Optimise and repeat until it converts

There is no one-size-fits-all GTM playbook. From Week 4 we run a weekly optimise-and-repeat cycle across ICPs, industries, messages, offers, channels, timing and landing pages, until we find the right way to get leads and turn them into paying customers. That is the main goal.

  1. Measure: leads, replies, demos and paying customers by channel and ICP.
  2. Learn: what is converting and what isn't.
  3. Optimise: fix targeting, messaging, timing and offers; switch off what doesn't work.
  4. Scale: put more volume behind what works.
  5. Repeat every week.
  • Some experiments will fail. That is part of the process, and every failure tells us where not to spend time and money.
  • Every experiment is logged with a clear verdict: scale / iterate / kill.
  • You see every experiment and its result in the weekly report.

4.4 Rollout plan

When What goes live "Done" check
Week 1: connect everything Kickoff and ICP/messaging sign-off; tracking (GA4, Tag Manager, pixels), CRM and the daily report bot (Telegram, or WhatsApp); Claude Code, 2 Grok bots and pre-warmed mailboxes; lead sources (ICP databases, Product Hunt, Google Maps); WhatsApp Business numbers; social profiles fixed and linked Every account and tool connected; the daily report arrives every morning
Week 2: outbound engines on ICP lead finder + cold email (30/day); Product Hunt daily launch outreach; Google Maps → email + WhatsApp Business outreach 30/day sending steadily, mailboxes healthy, first replies coming in
Week 3: inbound & social engines on LinkedIn (founder content, company pages, outbound); Instagram + X (content, comment-to-DM, social listening); WhatsApp AI SDR, nurture and demo reminders; website AI chat agent and SEO fixes All core automations running by the end of Week 3
Week 4 onward: optimise & repeat Weekly cycle: measure → learn → optimise → scale. Free tools, programmatic SEO, signal engines, paid ads, the partner program and webinars are added once the core is producing leads A repeatable path from lead → demo → paying customer

If a channel is clearly working, we put more volume behind it first.

4.5 What it runs on

The automations run on our own stack: Claude Code to build and run the automations, research leads, personalise outreach, draft content and write the reports, and Grok bots with pre-warmed mailboxes for cold email, plus the tools listed in Section 11. The engagement does not require any changes to the Celetel or CelChat platforms.

4.6 Sample: automations and routines running on our Grok bot

Below is a real example from one of our own live projects. Our Grok bot runs 12 routines on a schedule (daily, weekly and monthly), covering growth updates, X posts, directory submissions, SEO checks, newsletters and outreach drafts, plus a daily report on Telegram. Celetel's setup follows the same pattern, with its own routines for lead finding, outreach, content and reporting.

Sample: routines running on our Grok bot for one of our live projects (all times IST).

4.7 Sample result: a meeting booked within 1 week of setup

Here is a real result from the same system running for CryptoPrism (cryptoprism.io). Within 1 week of setup, an automated, personalised cold email to Spotware (the company behind the cTrader trading platform) got a reply from their Manager of Business Integrations asking for an intro call. Celetel's outreach runs on the same engine: ICP lead finding, personalised emails and fast follow-up.

Sample: Spotware's reply requesting an intro call, within 1 week of setting up outreach for cryptoprism.io.

5. Scope of Work: what we will do

The scope is organised into 12 workstreams. Each one is automated end to end. Humans (us) design, monitor, and optimise. Celetel's team only (a) approves brand content during the first 30 days and (b) takes the demos we book.

Workstream 1 — Foundation: tracking, analytics & CRM (Week 1)

  2. After the minimum term: the agreement continues month to month automatically.
  3. Ending the agreement: either party may end it with 30 days' written notice (email or WhatsApp is fine) after the minimum term. The fee for the notice period is payable.
  4. Handover on exit: on termination we hand over all workflows, data, content, documentation and access within 7 days of the final payment.

Scope & delivery

  1. Scope: the work is as described in Section 5. Anything outside it (e.g. a new brand, a new market, ad management at large budgets) is agreed separately through a written change request and may change the fee.
  2. Timelines depend on access: timelines start once the access and inputs in Section 8 are provided. Delays in access or approvals move timelines by the same amount.
  3. Approvals: Celetel approves brand content during the first 30 days. Content not reviewed within 2 business days may be published from approved templates only.
  4. Results: we commit to the work, the process, and full transparency on every number. Specific lead, demo or revenue numbers are not guaranteed, because they also depend on the market, product, pricing and how quickly sales follows up on leads. KPI targets are agreed together around Week 7 (Section 7).
  5. Sales follow-up: we book, brief and follow up. Celetel's team runs demos and closes deals, and updates outcomes in the CRM.

Ownership, confidentiality & compliance

  1. Ownership: all accounts, domains, content, data, automations and CRM records created for this engagement belong to Celetel.
  2. Confidentiality: both parties keep each other's business information, customer data and pricing confidential, during the engagement and for 2 years after it ends.
  3. Data & compliance: we follow the guardrails in Section 10 (WhatsApp, DLT, DPDP Act, email and platform rules). Celetel is responsible for the accuracy of its product claims and for the consents of its existing customer lists.
  4. Communication: daily report on Telegram (or WhatsApp), weekly report, monthly review call. Messages are answered within 1 business day.
  5. Fee review: the fee may be reviewed after the minimum term, or earlier if the scope expands, always with mutual agreement.
  6. Acceptance: approval by signature, or written confirmation on email or WhatsApp, counts as acceptance of this agreement.

14. Frequently asked questions

Is this a one-time fee? No. You pay a 50% advance (₹15,000) on approval and the balance (₹15,000) when the automations go live at the end of Week 3. From Month 2 it runs as a ₹30,000/month subscription, billed in advance.

When does the work start? Within 24 hours of approving this agreement and paying the 50% advance (₹15,000).

What does the ₹30,000 cover? Everything in Section 5: strategy, building and running the automations, content for LinkedIn, Instagram, X and WhatsApp, cold outreach (30 emails per day), Product Hunt and Google Maps outreach, website and analytics, experiments, and all reporting.

What is not included? Tool subscriptions (Claude Code, Grok bots and any other approved tools), ad spend, sales calls and closing, and product development on the Celetel/CelChat apps.

Why is there a 3-month minimum? Setup takes 3 weeks. After that, it takes several weekly optimise-and-repeat cycles to find what actually turns leads into paying customers. Three months is the minimum to see real results.

When will we see the first leads? Cold email goes live in Week 2, so the first replies and leads usually arrive in Weeks 2–3. By the end of Week 3 every core automation is running, and volume grows from there.

Do you guarantee a number of leads or customers? No agency can honestly guarantee that, because results also depend on the product, pricing and sales follow-up. What we guarantee is the work, the process, and that you see every number every day. KPI targets are agreed together around Week 7, based on real data.

How will we know what's happening? A daily report at 9:00 AM on Telegram (or WhatsApp, if a WhatsApp Business number is available), a weekly report every Monday, a monthly review call, and a live dashboard you can open any time.

Who owns the accounts, data and automations? Celetel does. Everything is set up under Celetel-owned accounts and handed over in full if the engagement ends.

Is our main domain or WhatsApp number at risk from cold outreach? No. Cold email goes from separate pre-warmed mailboxes on separate domains, and WhatsApp cold outreach uses a separate number. Celetel's main domain and main business WhatsApp numbers are never used for cold outreach.

What happens if a payment is late? After 7 days, work may pause until the payment is cleared. Nothing is deleted, and work resumes as soon as the payment is received.

How do we end the agreement? After the 3-month minimum, give 30 days' written notice on email or WhatsApp. We hand over everything within 7 days of the final payment.

Can we add more to the scope later? Yes. New work is agreed through a short written change request, and the fee is adjusted only if the scope grows significantly.

How do we pay? By bank transfer (NEFT / IMPS / RTGS) or UPI, using the payment details in Section 12. Please share the transaction reference once paid.

What do you need from us to get started? The access and inputs listed in Section 8: mainly logins and access, a WhatsApp number, brand assets, and a weekly 2-minute voice note from the founder.

  8. Day 30: first monthly report. The ₹30,000/month subscription starts from Month 2.

1. Design principles

  1. Revenue is the only goal. Every workflow must move a lead toward demo → paid. If a workflow can't be tied to a funnel metric, it doesn't ship.
  2. Dogfood everything. Celetel (WhatsApp, RCS, SMS, Voice, AI Agents) and CelChat (inbox, WebChat, Instagram) are the delivery rails for our own GTM. Every touchpoint doubles as a product demo.
  3. One data layer, two funnels. Celetel (CPaaS, usage revenue, India-first) and CelChat (inbox SaaS, seat revenue, global) get separate messaging and pipelines, but share accounts, contacts, signals, scoring and reporting.
  4. Signal > volume. We reach fewer people at the right moment (hiring, funding, CTWA ads, competitor pain, pricing-page visits) instead of spraying lists.
  5. Human-in-the-loop by exception. Automation does the work; humans approve brand content (first 30 days), handle demos, and review weekly quality samples.
  6. Compliance by design. Opt-in for WhatsApp API messaging, permission-first 1-to-1 WhatsApp cold outreach from a separate number, DLT for SMS, DPDP/GDPR consent logging, platform-safe pacing on LinkedIn/X.
  7. One automation at a time. Build → test small → measure → fix → lock in, then start the next. Full rollout takes a minimum of 1–2 months (Section 10).
  8. Experiment until it converts. Every workflow is an experiment until the data proves it turns leads into paying customers. We log, judge and iterate weekly (Section 8).

WF-01 — Tracking & attribution backbone

  • Trigger: every page view and event on celetel.com, celchat.com, app sign-up and demo pages.
  • Steps: GTM (web + server container) → GA4 events → Meta CAPI / LinkedIn CAPI / Google enhanced conversions → first-party cookie with UTM + click-ID storage (gclid, fbclid, li_fat_id) → passed into hidden form fields and sign-up payloads → written to the CRM contact as original source and latest source.
  • Output: every lead in the CRM carries first-touch and last-touch workflow IDs.
  • See: Section 6 (tracking plan).

WF-02 — Inbound lead capture → enrich → score → route

  • Triggers: contact form, /schedule-demo, /auth/register, CelChat /get-started, LinkedIn Lead Gen Form, Meta lead ad, CTWA chat, missed call, free-tool sign-up.
  • Steps:
    1. Webhook → n8n → dedupe against the CRM (email, phone, domain).
    2. Clay enrichment (company, size, tech stack, LinkedIn, title validation).
    3. Use the form data already captured (service interest + monthly traffic band) as a strong fit signal.
    4. Compute scores → set lifecycle stage.
    5. Instant WhatsApp from Celetel's number (template: welcome + "book a slot" button) within 60 seconds.
    6. Route: ≥ 75 → owner alert + call task; otherwise → nurture track by ICP.
  • KPI: speed-to-lead < 2 min, form → demo rate.

WF-03 — Website visitor reveal → alert → sequence

  • Trigger: an identified company visits ≥ 2 pages, or any high-intent page (/pricing, /pricing/template-pricing, comparison pages, /products/*).
  • Steps: reveal tool → n8n → match to ICP → find 2–3 decision-makers via Clay → add Intent: site_visit signal → if priority ≥ 75, alert sales with the pages viewed; else enrol in a "saw you were exploring X" LinkedIn + email sequence (no mention of tracking; content-led).
  • KPI: revealed accounts/week, revealed → meeting rate.

WF-04 — AI website agent

  • Stack: CelChat WebChat widget on both sites, powered by a Celetel AI Agent trained on product pages, pricing, FAQs, docs, case studies and the objection library.
  • Behaviour: proactive trigger on pricing page (after 20 seconds) and exit intent → answer questions → qualify (industry, use case, volume, timeline, role) → offer a demo slot or "send me the details on WhatsApp" (opt-in captured) → conversation transcript + qualification written to the CRM.
  • Handoff: human takeover in CelChat for priority accounts during business hours.
  • KPI: chats → qualified leads, chats → demos.

WF-05 — Founder voice-note → multi-channel content engine

  • Trigger: the founder sends a voice note (or a forwarded article/idea) to the GTM WhatsApp number, plus weekly scheduled content slots.
  • Steps:
    1. Celetel webhook → n8n → transcription → LLM extracts 3–6 ideas.
    2. Generate drafts in the founder voice profile (trained on past posts and messages): LinkedIn posts, X thread, IG carousel script, Reel script, newsletter section, blog outline.
    3. Creatives auto-generated from brand templates (Canva API / image generation for carousels and quote cards).
    4. Approval request sent on WhatsApp with one-tap ✅ / ✏️ / ❌ buttons (first 30 days mandatory, then optional per content pillar).
    5. Approved → scheduled at optimal times via the scheduler API, auto-UTM'd.
  • Content pillars: (1) industry playbooks, (2) WhatsApp/RCS/SMS economics, (3) product demos, (4) customer wins, (5) founder journey and opinions, (6) India CPaaS market and regulation news.
  • KPI: posts/week shipped, engagement rate, profile → site clicks, content-sourced leads.

WF-07 — LinkedIn engager harvesting → outbound

  • Senders: founder + 1–3 sales profiles (warmed up, completed, active).

WF-10 — X social listening + reply engine

  • KPI: relevant conversations joined/week, profile visits, X-sourced leads.

WF-11 — WhatsApp AI SDR + nurture journeys

  • Number: dedicated Celetel WhatsApp API number, inbox in CelChat.
  • AI SDR flow:
    Inbound message / CTWA click / opt-in
  → greet + identify brand interest (Celetel / CelChat)
  → qualify: industry, use case, monthly volume or agent count, timeline, role
  → answer from knowledge base (pricing, features, compliance, integrations)
  → score update in CRM
  → priority ≥ 75 → offer live call now / book slot → human takeover in CelChat
  → else → enrol in nurture journey

    • J-TRIAL: Day 0 welcome → Day 1 connect number guide → Day 2 template approval tips → Day 4 first campaign nudge → Day 7 setup-call offer → Day 12 plan recommendation → Day 14 expiry.
    • J-VERTICAL-{D2C|BFSI|RE|HEALTH|EDU|LOGI}: weekly vertical flow + mini case study + "experience it live" demo link.
    • J-POST-DEMO: recap → proposal → ROI sheet → payment link → follow-ups at 2/5/10 days.
  • "Experience it live": QR or link → user opts in → receives a real interactive flow on their phone (cart recovery, OTP with fallback, appointment booking, RCS rich card) → at the end, "Want this for your brand? Book 15 min."
  • Missed-call line: Celetel Voice number → missed call → instant WhatsApp + callback task in the CRM.
  • KPI: conversations → qualified, opt-in rate, journey → demo rate, template read rates.

WF-12 — Demo booking, reminders, no-show recovery

  • Steps: booking (Cal.com / HubSpot Meetings, round-robin by vertical) → confirmation on WhatsApp + email → reminders at 24h (WhatsApp), 1h (RCS/SMS), 10 min (WhatsApp with join link) → pre-demo brief to the rep (AI research agent: company summary, stack, competitor, estimated volume, suggested plan, talking points) → no-show → auto-reschedule message within 5 minutes + 2 follow-ups.
  • KPI: show rate (target > 75%), reschedule recovery rate.

WF-13 — ICP lead finder + cold email engine (30/day) + AI reply handling

  • Infra: 2 Grok bot seats with 2 pre-warmed mailboxes on secondary domains (never the main celetel.com / celchat.com domain), with SPF/DKIM/DMARC, ongoing warm-up and inbox rotation.
  • Daily volume: 30 emails/day across both mailboxes (~15 each), spread across working hours. The cap includes follow-ups, so the queue mixes new first touches with due follow-ups. Raise the cap only after 2+ weeks of bounce < 2%, no spam-folder placement in seed tests, and a stable reply rate.
  • Automatic ICP lead finder (runs nightly, orchestrated by Claude Code + n8n):
    ICP definitions (Workstream 2) + yesterday's learnings
  → pull candidates (Apollo / Sales Nav / signals / WF-31 Product Hunt / WF-32 Google Maps)
  → dedupe vs CRM + global suppression list
  → enrich (company, size, stack, decision-maker, verified email)
  → score Fit + Intent → keep top N to fill tomorrow's 30-slot queue
  → LLM writes a personalised opener per lead from signal context
  → push to Grok bot sequence + log in CRM
  • Sequence (default): Day 0 personalised first touch → Day 3 value follow-up (use-case or cost insight) → Day 7 proof (mini case study / "we built your flow" mockup) → Day 12 breakup. Stops on reply.
  • Personalisation: LLM opener using signal context (Product Hunt launch, Google Maps category/rating, hiring, funding, CTWA ads, OTP complaints, tech stack).
  • Reply handling: AI classifies → interested (booking link + CRM SQL + WhatsApp alert to sales), not now (snooze to date), referral (new contact + sequence), objection (rep draft), unsubscribe (global suppression).
  • KPI: 30 sends/day delivered, deliverability > 95%, bounce < 2%, positive reply rate, meetings per 100 sends.

WF-14 — "We built your flow" account mockup generator

  • Trigger: account priority ≥ 75 in ICP A (D2C), C (Real Estate) or D (Healthcare).
  • Steps: scrape logo + 3 products (Shopify products.json / site images) → render a WhatsApp chat mockup (cart recovery / site-visit booking / appointment reminder) from an HTML template → export PNG + personalised landing page (celetel.com/for/{brand}) → insert into LinkedIn DM / email step.
  • KPI: reply rate vs control.

WF-15 — Meta Ad Library CTWA advertiser miner

  • Schedule: daily.
  • Steps: query Meta Ad Library (India, active ads, CTWA objective/indicators) → extract advertiser page + domain → dedupe → enrich → tag signal: ctwa_ads → route to sequence: "You're paying for WhatsApp conversations. Here's how to convert more of them automatically."
  • KPI: new CTWA advertisers/week, meetings.

WF-16 — Competitor widget detection → switch campaign

  • Steps: crawl target domains (and BuiltWith lists) for competitor scripts, widgets and wa.me patterns → tag competitor → switch sequence with a migration checklist, cost-comparison calculator, and "we migrate you free" offer (if Celetel approves).
  • KPI: switch-campaign meetings, competitor displacement wins.

WF-17 — Play Store OTP complaint miner

  • Steps: weekly scrape of reviews for top Indian fintech, lending, e-commerce, gaming and edtech apps → filter "OTP not received / OTP late / OTP not coming" → count + sample quotes → tag the account → outreach to CTO/product head with "X users reported OTP failures in the last 30 days. Here's multi-channel OTP with automatic fallback."
  • KPI: BFSI/fintech meetings.

WF-18 — Hiring + funding signal monitor

  • Sources: LinkedIn Jobs, Naukri, Indeed, company careers pages; Inc42, Entrackr, YourStory, Tracxn, Crunchbase feeds.
  • Rules: roles matching CRM/retention/WhatsApp marketing/chat support/contact centre → +20 intent; funding in the last 90 days → +15.
  • Action: timed sequence referencing the trigger ("Congrats on the Series A. Scaling support usually breaks WhatsApp first…").

WF-19 — Vertical scrapers

  • RERA: new project registrations (MahaRERA, K-RERA, HRERA, etc.) → developer → Real Estate sequence (lead response + site-visit automation).
  • Google Maps: see WF-32 (email + WhatsApp Business outreach).
  • New Shopify stores (India): store-lead feeds → PLG offer (Starter plan + free template pack).

WF-20 — Competitor review + complaint radar

  • Sources: G2, Capterra, Play Store, Trustpilot, Reddit, X for Wati, Interakt, AiSensy, Gallabox, Gupshup, respond.io, Trengo, etc.
  • Action: negative reviewer's company → identify decision-maker → empathetic switch outreach + comparison page link. Monthly "competitor weakness" report feeds messaging and comparison pages.

WF-21 — Programmatic SEO page factory

  • Data sources: industries × cities, competitor list, use-case template library, Celetel pricing by country, integration list.
  • Page templates:
    • /whatsapp-api-for/{industry} and /whatsapp-api-for/{industry}/{city}
    • /alternatives/{competitor} and /compare/celetel-vs-{competitor}
    • /whatsapp-templates/{use-case} (with copy-ready examples)
    • /whatsapp-pricing/{country}
    • /integrations/{tool}
  • Pipeline: dataset → LLM drafts unique sections per page (not thin spin) → human QA sample (10%) → publish via CMS/static build → internal-link graph → indexing via Search Console API → track rankings weekly.
  • Prerequisite: CelChat moved to pre-rendered/static HTML (see SOW, finding #4).
  • KPI: indexed pages, organic sessions, pSEO-sourced sign-ups.

WF-22 — Free tools → lead capture

  • Tools: WhatsApp cost calculator, WhatsApp vs SMS vs RCS ROI calculator, wa.me link + QR generator, template preview/checker, RCS card preview, DLT template formatter.
  • Capture: result emailed/WhatsApped (opt-in) → CRM → J-VERTICAL nurture by selected industry.
  • KPI: tool sessions, tool → lead conversion, backlinks earned.

WF-23 — Partner / reseller recruitment

  • Sources: Shopify Partners, Zoho Partners, HubSpot Solutions directories, Clutch/GoodFirms digital agency lists.
  • Offer: white-label Celetel + recurring margin.
  • Flow: sequence → partner call → partner portal (onboarding kit, demo account, co-branded collateral) → partner-sourced deals tracked with partner IDs → monthly partner leaderboard.
  • KPI: partners signed, partner-sourced MRR.

WF-24 — Event & webinar automation

  • Events: scrape exhibitor/speaker lists 4–6 weeks before → pre-event outreach ("meeting at the venue?") → on-site QR → "experience it live" WhatsApp demo → post-event sequence.
  • Webinars: monthly vertical webinar → registration page → WhatsApp + email reminders → replay distribution → attendee scoring (attended / stayed > 30 min / asked question).

WF-25 — Paid ads + offline conversion sync

  • Campaigns: Google Search (intent + competitor + brand defence), Meta CTWA + lead ads + retargeting, LinkedIn ABM + Thought Leader Ads + Lead Gen Forms, X retargeting.
  • Audiences synced daily from the CRM: MQL list (retarget), customer list (exclude + lookalike), revealed accounts (LinkedIn company targeting).
  • Offline conversions: CRM stage changes (MQL, SQL, Demo held, Paid with value) → Google Ads / Meta CAPI / LinkedIn CAPI daily, so bidding optimises for revenue.
  • Guardrail rules: CPA above target for 3 days → pause ad set; ROAS winners → +20% budget; anomaly alert to the WhatsApp digest.

WF-26 — Trial activation → PQL → paid

  • Events required from apps: signup, number_connected, template_submitted, template_approved, first_campaign_sent, agent_invited, channel_connected (CelChat), messages_sent_7d, plan_viewed, plan_purchased.
  • Rules:
    • No number_connected after 24h → setup help message + video.
    • template_approved but no first_campaign_sent after 48h → campaign idea pack.
    • PQL = (first_campaign_sent AND messages_sent_7d ≥ threshold) OR agents ≥ 3 → sales alert + personal outreach.
    • Trial Day 10–14 → plan recommendation based on actual usage + payment link.
  • KPI: activation rate, trial → paid rate, time-to-first-value.

WF-27 — Expansion, cross-sell, churn-risk, win-back

  • Expansion: usage ≥ 80% of plan → upgrade nudge; seats full → add-seat offer.
  • Cross-sell: Celetel customer with high inbound reply volume → CelChat; CelChat customer on Twilio/Vonage/Infobip/Bird with India traffic → Celetel cost comparison.
  • Churn-risk: usage drops > 40% week-over-week, failed payments, low CSAT → CSM task + save sequence.
  • Win-back: lapsed trials at 30/60/90 days with "what's new" + offer; churned accounts quarterly.

WF-28 — Reviews + referrals engine

  • Trigger: happy-customer signals (consistent usage 60+ days, positive CSAT, support ticket resolved fast).
  • Action: WhatsApp ask → G2/Capterra/Google review link → thank-you + referral link → referral tracking → automatic reward/credit.

WF-29 — Reporting

  • Daily digest (09:00 IST, via Celetel WhatsApp template + email):
    📊 Celetel GTM — Daily Digest (Tue, 10 Nov)
Website: 1,240 sessions (▲12%) · Sign-ups: 18 · Demos booked: 6
Outbound: 30 emails sent · 4 replies (2 positive) · PH launches contacted: 12 · Maps WhatsApp chats: 6
New leads: 54 · MQLs: 14 · SQLs: 5 · New paid: 2 (₹11,998 MRR)
🔥 Hot accounts: Acme Lending (pricing ×3), ShopX (CTWA ads + demo booked), Zeta Health
⚠️ Needs you: approve 4 founder posts · 1 enterprise lead waiting > 1h
▶ Dashboard: <link>
    (Illustrative numbers only.)
  • Weekly report (Monday, PDF + email): funnel by stage and brand, channel table (leads, MQL, SQL, paid, CAC), top content, outbound stats, experiments and verdicts, pipeline forecast, next-week plan.
  • Monthly business review: revenue attribution (first/last/multi-touch), ICP performance, budget reallocation, roadmap.
  • Real-time alerts: priority ≥ 75 account activity, enterprise sign-up, positive reply, SLA breach on inbound.
  • Build: n8n cron → queries warehouse + GA4 API + platform APIs → LLM writes the narrative "what changed and why" → Celetel WhatsApp API send + email + PDF render.

WF-30 — Data hygiene, dedupe, consent & suppression

  • Nightly dedupe (domain, email, phone E.164), job-change detection, bounce/invalid cleanup.
  • Global suppression list across all channels (unsubscribes, opt-outs, existing customers in prospecting flows, competitors).
  • Consent ledger: channel, source, timestamp, proof. WhatsApp API sends (nurture, broadcasts) are blocked unless consent exists. WF-32 cold WhatsApp messages run only from the separate outreach number, and any "no" or "stop" is added to the global suppression list immediately.
  • DLT template registry check before any SMS send.

WF-31 — Product Hunt daily launch outreach

  • Trigger: daily (morning IST, after the Product Hunt day rolls over), via our Product Hunt extension.
  • Steps:
    1. Collect every product launched that day: product name, tagline, category, website, upvotes, makers/hunters, maker profile links.
    2. Filter: drop non-software, already-contacted and suppressed products; tag by category (SaaS, fintech, e-commerce tools, AI apps, dev tools…).
    3. Enrich makers: verified email, LinkedIn, X handle.
    4. Match the pitch:
      • Celetel: OTP / verification, onboarding and notification flows on WhatsApp, SMS and RCS for their new users.
      • CelChat: one inbox for user conversations as launch traffic grows (WhatsApp, Instagram, WebChat).
    5. LLM writes a congratulations-plus-value first line referencing their tagline ("Congrats on launching X today. Most launch-day sign-ups never verify their email; WhatsApp OTP fixes that…").
    6. Queue into WF-13 (counts toward the 30/day cap) + same-day X/LinkedIn engagement on their launch post.
  • KPI: launches collected/day, contactable %, reply rate, PH-sourced demos and trials.

WF-32 — Google Maps leads → email + WhatsApp Business outreach

  • Source: our Google Maps lead lists / scraper, run by category × city batches (e.g. "diagnostic lab × Pune", "coaching institute × Jaipur", "real estate agent × Bengaluru").
  • Fields captured: business name, category, website, email, phone, address, city, rating, review count, Maps URL.
  • Steps:
    1. Clean and verify: email verification; phone normalised to E.164 and checked for WhatsApp availability.
    2. Enrich from the website where present (owner/manager name, social links, existing chat widget).
    3. Score (category fit, review count as a size proxy, multi-location = chain bonus).
    4. Email path: queue into WF-13 with an industry-specific sequence.
    5. WhatsApp path: personalised 1-to-1 message from the dedicated outreach number (never Celetel's main API number), at a low daily volume with randomised spacing. Permission-first opener → on "yes", send a 30-second demo video or the "experience it live" flow (WF-11) → replies land in CelChat → AI agent qualifies → hot leads get a demo slot.
    6. No reply after 1 follow-up, or any "no" → stop and suppress.
  • Industry offers: clinics/labs (appointment reminders, report delivery), coaching (fee reminders, admission enquiries), real estate (60-second enquiry replies, site-visit booking), restaurants/retail (offers to past customers, review requests), dealerships (service reminders).
  • KPI: leads per batch, email and WhatsApp reply rates, conversations → demos, outreach-number health (blocks/reports).

6. Tracking plan (GA4 + CRM)

6.1 Events

Event Where Key parameters
page_view All pages brand, page_type (home/product/pricing/solution/blog/pseo/tool)
cta_click All CTAs cta_id, cta_text, location
pricing_view /pricing, /pricing/template-pricing brand, currency
pricing_toggle Billing period / currency toggles period, currency
contact_submit /contact service, monthly_traffic, country
demo_booked /schedule-demo, booking tool brand, source_wf
signup_start / signup_complete /auth/register, /get-started brand, plan
whatsapp_click wa.me / CTWA buttons location
chat_started / chat_qualified WebChat brand, qualified
tool_used / tool_lead Free tools tool_id
content_download Gated assets asset_id
trial_activated App (server-side) brand, channel_connected
purchase App (server-side) plan, value, currency

6.2 UTM convention

utm_source = platform (linkedin, instagram, x, whatsapp, email, google, meta, partner) · utm_medium = organic | paid | outbound | nurture | referral · utm_campaign = <WF-ID>_<short-name> · utm_content = variant/creative ID · utm_term = keyword/persona. All links are generated by a shared link builder (n8n endpoint / sheet) so naming is never manual.

6.3 Attribution

  • CRM stores first touch, last touch, and all touches per contact.
  • Reports show first-touch (what creates demand), last-touch (what converts), and a W-shaped multi-touch view for budget decisions.

7. Content system

  • Brand voice profiles: Celetel (confident, enterprise-reliable, India-proud, numbers-driven), CelChat (friendly, modern, CX-team empathy), Founder (personal, opinionated, builder).
  • Asset library: flow templates per industry, product screenshots, approved stats (single source of truth, fixing the current inconsistencies), customer quotes, objection-handling answers.
  • Repurposing chain: 1 founder voice note or 1 blog → 3 LinkedIn posts + 1 X thread + 1 IG carousel + 1 Reel script + 1 newsletter block + 1 WhatsApp Channel update.
  • Quality gates: LLM fact-check against the approved claims library, banned-claims list (no unverifiable stats), plagiarism check, human approval queue.

8. Experiment framework

  • Cadence: 2–4 experiments/week across channels, logged in an experiment board.
  • Template: hypothesis → metric → variant → sample size / duration → result → verdict (scale / iterate / kill).
  • Mindset: we expect many experiments to fail. The job is to find, as fast as possible, the ICP × message × channel combinations that turn into paying customers, then scale only those.
  • First experiments (cold outbound, Weeks 2–6):
    1. ICP A vs B vs C vs Product Hunt startups vs Google Maps SMBs → positive reply rate and demo rate per segment.
    2. Celetel pitch (cost/OTP/campaigns) vs CelChat pitch (one inbox) for the same segment → reply rate.
    3. Short plain-text vs mockup-image first touch → reply rate.
    4. "Book a demo" vs "Want a 30-second demo on WhatsApp?" CTA → conversion to conversation.
    5. Google Maps: email-first vs WhatsApp-first → conversations started per 100 leads.
  • Later experiments:
    1. WhatsApp-first vs email-first follow-up after a form fill → demo rate.
    2. "We built your flow" mockup vs plain-text first touch → reply rate.
    3. Pricing page: monthly vs yearly default → sign-up rate.
    4. Founder Thought Leader Ad vs company-page ad → cost per MQL.
    5. Comment-to-DM keyword variants → DM conversion.
    6. Live "experience it" demo CTA vs "book a demo" CTA → SQL rate.

9. Security, access & ownership

  • All accounts are created under Celetel-owned logins/business managers; we receive role-based access (no shared passwords; SSO/2FA where available).
  • API keys are stored in a secrets manager / n8n credential vault, never in docs or chats.
  • The warehouse is hosted in India (or a region of Celetel's choice), with access logs.
  • On exit: full export of workflows (n8n JSON), data, content and documentation handed over.

10. Build plan: one automation at a time

Rule: a new automation starts only when the previous one passes its "done" check. Full rollout takes a minimum of 1–2 months; the order can change if experiments show a channel is clearly winning.

Step Timing Automation (workflows) "Done" check before the next step
0 Week 1 Access, audit, ICP workshop, claims library; Claude Code + n8n + warehouse set up; Grok bot seats + pre-warmed mailboxes connected Tools live, ICPs and messaging approved
1 Weeks 1–2 Foundation: WF-01 tracking, WF-02 inbound capture, WF-30 hygiene, CRM pipelines, WF-29 daily digest v1, social profiles fixed and linked Every lead has a source; the daily report arrives every morning
2 Weeks 2–3 WF-13 ICP lead finder + cold email, 30/day 30/day sending steadily for 1 week, bounce < 2%, replies flowing into the CRM
3 Weeks 3–4 WF-31 Product Hunt daily outreach (feeds WF-13) Daily launch list collected and contacted automatically
4 Weeks 4–5 WF-32 Google Maps → email + WhatsApp outreach First city × category batches done; WhatsApp replies landing in CelChat; outreach number healthy
5 Weeks 5–6 LinkedIn: WF-05 founder content, WF-06 company pages, WF-07 + WF-08 outbound Posting on schedule; accept and reply rates measured
6 Weeks 6–7 Instagram + X: WF-09 comment-to-DM, WF-10 listening + replies DMs and mentions routed to CelChat automatically
7 Weeks 7–8 WhatsApp conversion layer: WF-11 AI SDR + nurture, WF-12 demo reminders, WF-26 trial → paid (needs app events) Inbound leads qualified 24/7; demo show rate tracked
8 Month 2–3 Website: WF-04 AI chat, SEO fixes, CelChat pre-rendering, WF-22 free tools, WF-21 first pSEO batch, WF-03 visitor reveal Pages indexed; website leads attributed
9 Month 3+ Scale layer: WF-14–WF-20 signal engines, WF-25 ads + offline conversions, WF-23 partners, WF-24 webinars, WF-27 expansion, WF-28 reviews/referrals Only after the core engine produces leads reliably
Ongoing From Step 2 Weekly experiments (Section 8), ICP refresh, scale winners, kill losers A proven lead → paying-customer path

11. Open questions for kickoff

  1. Which CRM is in use today (if any), and who owns it?
  2. Can the app teams send product events (WF-26) via webhook, or should we read from the database/analytics?
  3. Exact relationship and positioning between Celetel and CelChat (separate pricing? separate sales team? CelChat Inc. entity for international?).
  4. Which proof numbers are current and approved (businesses, clients, messages/day)?
  5. Official LinkedIn, Instagram and X handles for both brands (none are linked from the websites today).
  6. Priority ICPs and geographies for the first 90 days.
  7. Ad budget range and tool budget approval process.
  8. Sales capacity: how many demos/week can the team take, and in which languages?
  9. Any existing customer case studies or logos we can use with consent?
  10. Willingness to offer a free migration / switch incentive for competitor users.
  11. Confirm the Claude Code plan and the 2 Grok bot seats (with pre-warmed mailboxes); agree on the sending domains to use.
  12. Who will own the separate WhatsApp outreach number for Google Maps leads?

documents.summary: First-90-day ICPs and messages for Celetel and CelChat, based on your 18 November answers. Delhi NCR, Mumbai and Bengaluru first in India; UK, then UAE/GCC, then a careful US motion abroad. Please approve the priority and the draft switch offer.
documents.html:
Ideal customers and messages

Celetel × CelChat — GTM Autopilot
Prepared for Lalit, Founder — Celetel (incl. CelChat)
Prepared by Ranjeet Ratan — Limedock
Date: 25 November 2026
Status: For approval (first 90 days)
Companion to the Scope of Work (4 Nov 2026) and GTM design doc

This document replaces the tracker placeholder “Ideal customers and messages.” It is a research-backed draft for Lalit’s approval. It does not invent customer names, employee counts, or market sizes. Where a figure comes from the Scope of Work, it is labelled as a hypothesis (to be checked against closed-won data, which has not been shared yet). Everything else is cited.

1. How to read this

Two products, two buyers, one data layer — as already agreed in the SoW:

  • Celetel is the India-first CPaaS (WhatsApp Business API, RCS, DLT SMS, Voice, AI Agents, campaigns). Revenue is platform subscription plus usage. Primary buyers: founders, CMOs, growth/CRM heads, CTOs and product heads (OTP and notifications).
  • CelChat is the omnichannel inbox (WhatsApp, Instagram, RCS, WebChat, Gmail) with bring-your-own provider (Twilio, Vonage, Infobip, Bird, and others). Revenue is seat/workspace subscription; channel costs are separate. Primary buyers: heads of CX/support, contact-centre managers, D2C ops leads.

On 18 November 2026 (6:19–6:21 PM IST) Lalit confirmed the first-90-day focus in the tracker:

  • Celetel: D2C and e-commerce in India.
  • CelChat: support teams already on Twilio, Infobip or similar, abroad.
  • Separate pricing, same sales team, no bundle today; India company for India, UK company for international clients.
  • Up to 20 demos a week, Hindi and English, with a preference for automated / self-serve demos across timezones.
  • A competitor switch / free-migration offer is not approved yet (“Can plan”).
  • Website proof numbers are not approved; both published sets are wrong. Do not use them in outreach until Lalit signs off a realistic set.

2. First 90 days: recommended priority

Rank Segment Product Why this order When to work it
1 A. D2C & e-commerce (India) Celetel + CelChat Lalit’s confirmed focus. Largest reachable list (Shopify/WooCommerce stores), clear pains (cart, COD/RTO, Instagram DMs), and both products can be sold. Week 2 lists and outbound first
2 G. Support-heavy teams on Twilio / Infobip / Vonage / Bird (global) CelChat Lalit’s confirmed international focus. CelChat is built to sit on those providers. Better fit for UK/UAE (and carefully the US) than a Celetel marketing-blast pitch. Week 2–3, in parallel with A
3 H. Competitor switchers Both Overlaps A and G. WATI, Interakt, AiSensy, Gallabox, Gupshup, respond.io, Trengo and similar are already named in the SoW. Strong hook if Lalit approves a migration offer. Same lists as A and G; messaging variant
4 C. Real estate (India) Celetel + AI Agents Fast enquiry-reply and site-visit use case is already on celetel.com. Google Maps and RERA lists are ready-made. From Week 3, after A/G lists are running
5 I. Channel partners Celetel white label Multiplier: Shopify, Zoho and HubSpot agencies in the same Indian metros. Not day-one outbound volume. Week 4–6, once a partner one-pager exists
6 D. Healthcare (India) Celetel Appointment and report use cases are clear. Hospital and diagnostic chains cluster in the same metros. Proof/compliance will matter; we do not yet have case studies. Later in the 90 days
7 E. EdTech & coaching (India) Celetel + CelChat Fee reminders and admissions-season lead handling. Google Maps coverage is good. Smaller first-wave than A. Later in the 90 days / seasonally
8 B. BFSI & fintech (India) Celetel High value (OTP, EMI, KYC), but the SoW itself notes that BFSI and enterprise buyers need proof before booking a demo. We have no approved logos or numbers yet. After proof pack exists
9 F. Logistics & travel Celetel Real use case (WISMO, booking confirmations). Deprioritised only because A/G are confirmed and lists are harder to build cleanly in week 1. After the core engine is live

3. Where to sell first (geos), and why

India (Celetel primary; CelChat as the inbox upsell)

Start in Delhi NCR, Mumbai and Bengaluru, then add Pune, Hyderabad, Chennai, Ahmedabad, Surat and Jaipur.

Evidence:

  • Inc42’s D2C 3.0 Report 2026: Delhi NCR, Mumbai and Bengaluru together took 89% of India’s ~$10 bn D2C funding from 2015 to Q1 2026. Delhi NCR led ($3.5 bn, 434 deals), then Bengaluru ($3.4 bn, 342 deals) and Mumbai ($2 bn, 362+ deals). Pune was the top emerging hub ($554 mn, 32 deals). Mumbai was the fastest-growing of the three (27% funding CAGR, 2020–25). Source: https://inc42.com/buzz/delhi-ncr-emerges-as-indias-top-d2c-hub/
  • Merchant Data (updated November 2026): 166,337 live single-brand Indian D2C stores. Of stores with a known city, Delhi NCR is about 1 in 5 (18.9%). Top cities: Delhi 18,970; Mumbai 12,626; Bengaluru 9,575; then Surat, Jaipur, Gurugram, Hyderabad, Chennai, Pune, Ahmedabad. Shopify powers 60.6% of live D2C stores and WooCommerce 32.7% (93.3% combined) — which matches the SoW’s Shopify/WooCommerce hypothesis. Source: https://merchantdata.in/insights/indian-d2c-statistics
  • Store Leads (updated 20 Nov 2026): 131,150 live Shopify stores in India. City counts it publishes: Mumbai 10,629; New Delhi 8,727; Bengaluru 8,168. State counts: Maharashtra 21,182; Delhi 15,983; Gujarat 13,192; Uttar Pradesh 11,994. Source: https://storeleads.app/reports/shopify/IN/top-stores
  • WhatsApp is the default business chat channel in India: Meta cites a Kantar 2025 finding that 91% of online adults in India chat with a business weekly (Meta, May 2026). Source: https://replykit.app/blog/whatsapp-business-statistics and Meta’s Kantar “State of Business Messaging” research (22 markets, Apr–Sep 2025): https://whatsappbusiness.com/resources/resource-library/state-of-business-messaging/
  • Celetel is incorporated in Noida, bills in INR, publishes DLT-compliant SMS rates, and is set up for this market (https://www.celetel.com/pricing).

Do not treat “₹1–100 Cr GMV” as a verified fact. It is the SoW’s starting hypothesis for ICP A, to be checked against closed-won data.

United Kingdom (CelChat primary; Celetel for India-bound or UK-originated traffic)

First international market.

Evidence:

  • Lalit: “we have 1 company each registered in India and UK. UK for international clients.” Companies House confirms CELETEL TECHNOLOGIES LTD (14055426), Active, London registered office, director Lalit Upadhyay: https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/14055426
  • DataReportal and GWI, Q1 2025 (internet users 16+ who used WhatsApp in the past month), as compiled by QuickWA: UK 81%, versus USA 30.1% and India 82.9%. Source: https://quickwa.com/blog/whatsapp-business-api-statistics-2026
  • Pricing headroom versus India is real on Meta’s own rate card (effective 1 October 2026, checked 20 Nov 2026 by Flowcall): India marketing ₹0.8631 (~$0.0118) vs United Kingdom marketing £0.0458 (~$0.0635); utility/auth/service India ₹0.115 (~$0.0014) vs UK £0.0159 (~$0.022). Source: https://www.flowcall.co/blog/whatsapp-business-api-pricing and Meta’s pricing documentation. This supports Ranjeet’s 3 Nov point that international can be sold at a higher rate, and Lalit’s “separate pricing… so that the client pays more.”
  • English-language sales and demos (Lalit: Hindi and English) work without a new language motion. Automated / self-serve demos matter here because of timezone overlap with India.

UAE and GCC (CelChat, and Celetel where WhatsApp/RCS/SMS routes are quoted)

Second international wave, especially travel, real estate and bilingual sales teams.

Evidence:

  • respond.io’s 2025 State of Business Messaging (7 Oct 2025): EMEA accounted for 41% of global business-messaging adoption, led by the UAE (22% of EMEA share) and Saudi Arabia (10%). WhatsApp was the top business messaging channel in that report. Source: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/10/07/3162621/0/en/business-messaging-adoption-surged-53-in-2025-respond-io-report-finds.html
  • Meta list rates (1 Oct 2026): UAE marketing AED 0.2115 (~$0.0576); Saudi marketing SAR 0.2159 — several times India’s marketing rate. Source: https://www.flowcall.co/blog/whatsapp-business-api-pricing
  • Independent 2026 provider round-ups describe UAE adoption as heavily driven by real estate and travel Click-to-WhatsApp ads, with Arabic/English templates as table stakes. Source: https://oncloudapi.com/blogs/best-whatsapp-business-api-providers-in-2026-pakistan-uae-india-bangladesh-uk-usa-canada-compared
  • Celetel already attended Capacity Dubai (Capacity 2k25), per the company LinkedIn page — a relevant partner/industry event, not a customer proof point.

United States (CelChat only, and only with a careful offer)

There are many Twilio-using support teams in the US, but WhatsApp is not the default US consumer app, and marketing outreach to US numbers is constrained.

Evidence:

  • Twilio FY2025 10-K: United States 64% of revenue ($3.247 bn of $5.067 bn); International 36% ($1.820 bn). That is why US support/engineering teams show up often in Twilio stacks — not because US consumers live in WhatsApp. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1447669/000144766926000021/R84.htm
  • Pew Research Center, 2025: 32% of US adults use WhatsApp; 56% of Hispanic adults. Source: https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/2025/11/20/americans-social-media-use-2025/
  • Flowcall (facts checked 20 Nov 2026 against Meta’s card): “WhatsApp doesn’t currently deliver marketing templates to US numbers.” OnCloudAPI similarly notes standard marketing templates have been paused for US recipients, with Marketing Messages Lite as the alternative. Do not pitch Celetel marketing campaigns into the US until this is re-checked at send time. CelChat (shared inbox, support, utility, cross-border and diaspora use) is the safer US offer.

Southeast Asia (second 90 days unless a warm lead appears)

Strong WhatsApp usage, but not Lalit’s stated first focus.

  • DataReportal/GWI Q1 2025 via QuickWA: Indonesia 91.3% of internet users 16+ used WhatsApp in the past month. Source: https://quickwa.com/blog/whatsapp-business-api-statistics-2026
  • respond.io 2025: APAC business-messaging growth led by Malaysia (25%), Singapore (20%) and Thailand (9%). Source: the GlobeNewswire item above.
  • Treat SEA as a CelChat expansion after UK/UAE lists are running, unless a partner or inbound lead appears earlier.

4. Segment profiles

1) ICP A — D2C & e-commerce brands (India) — first priority

Who (hypothesis + what we can evidence)
Shopify or WooCommerce brands selling direct to Indian consumers. The SoW hypothesis is ₹1–100 Cr GMV; that number is unverified until we see closed-won data. Merchant Data and Store Leads show a very large store universe (see geos above). Team size is not published in a form we can cite; outreach should assume a founder, or a small growth / CRM / retention team, and be corrected once Lalit shares won-deal examples.

Buyers and triggers
Founder, Growth/Retention head, CRM manager (SoW). Pains the SoW and celetel.com already use, and that we should keep: cart abandonment, COD / return-to-origin losses, Instagram DM overload, order updates, Click-to-WhatsApp ads that dump into a messy inbox.

India vs global
India first, with Delhi NCR, Mumbai and Bengaluru as the starting cities; then Pune, Hyderabad, Chennai, Ahmedabad, Surat, Jaipur. CelChat is the upsell when Instagram DMs and WhatsApp support sit in two places.

Where they hang out (only communities and events we could verify)

  • D2C Insider (states 7,000+ brand founders; summits and CXO meets): https://www.d2cinsider.com/
  • Get Into D2C (WhatsApp community for Indian D2C founders; site states 200+ founders and operators): https://getintod2c.in/community/
  • groD2C (Bengaluru-based community of D2C founders; mixers, webinars, events): https://in.linkedin.com/showcase/grod2c/
  • ShopBrew (Shopify D2C meetups in Coimbatore, plus a Shopify podcast): https://shopbrew.co/
  • r/EcommerceIndia (active Indian ecommerce founder threads, including founder-only group invites): https://www.reddit.com/r/EcommerceIndia/
  • Trade press Indian D2C and startup buyers already read: Inc42, YourStory, Entrackr.
  • Events with dates we could confirm: India D2C Summit, 25–26 November 2026, Andaz Aerocity, New Delhi (agenda PDF: https://imagesretaillive.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Agenda-India-D2C-Summit-1.pdf) — this is happening as the engagement starts; useful for attendee/speaker lists even if exhibition is too late. eTailVerse Mumbai, 3 December 2026 (Shopify-backed commerce series that already ran in Delhi and in Bengaluru on 17 September 2026; GreenHonchos / Nitro Commerce posts). Shop Quest 2026 was at JW Marriott Bengaluru on 3 October 2026 (past; useful as a recurring-format / organiser lead).

How to find lists

  • Shopify store directories: Store Leads India report (link above); Merchant Data (https://merchantdata.in/).
  • Shopify App Store reviewers and install bases of WhatsApp apps, including WATI (https://apps.shopify.com/wati-abandonedcart-recovery) and Interakt (https://apps.shopify.com/interakt-sales, https://apps.shopify.com/interakt-marketing).
  • Technographic signals: Shopify or WooCommerce on the site; wa.me / Click-to-WhatsApp buttons; WATI and Interakt both publish website chat widgets whose scripts can be detected (WATI Growth Widget help: https://support.wati.io/en/articles/18453925-how-to-set-up-a-growth-widget-on-your-website; Interakt widget: https://www.interakt.shop/resource-center/whatspp-crm-shared-team-inbox-add-whatsapp-chat-widget/). Use BuiltWith / Wappalyzer-class tools as planned in the design doc; do not claim a exact public count of WATI or Interakt customers unless we pull a fresh export.
  • Meta Ad Library: brands running Click-to-WhatsApp ads in India.
  • Google Maps: retail and brand storefronts in the three metros (secondary to store directories for this ICP).
  • Job posts on LinkedIn Jobs and Naukri for “CRM manager”, “retention”, “WhatsApp marketing”, “community manager (D2C)”.
  • Product Hunt: new commerce and messaging tools (and the brands launching them).

Core message / offer
Celetel: recover carts and confirm COD on WhatsApp (and RCS where the handset allows) without adding another disconnected inbox. CelChat: one thread for WhatsApp + Instagram DMs + web chat, so “DM to order” comments do not get lost. If Lalit approves a switch offer: migrate templates and the current WhatsApp number from WATI / Interakt / AiSensy, with a short cost comparison against current BSP + tool fees. Do not use unverified “5,000+ businesses” style proof. Use a product demo (or the self-serve demo Lalit wants) and transparent India pricing (Starter ₹1,599 / Growth ₹2,999 / Business ₹5,999 plus usage, from https://www.celetel.com/pricing).

2) ICP G — Support-heavy teams already on Twilio, Infobip, Vonage or Bird (global) — first priority, international

Who (SoW hypothesis)
Support or contact-centre teams of about 5–200 agents (SoW figure; not independently verified) who already buy messaging from Twilio, Vonage, Infobip or Bird. CelChat’s own site positions exactly this “bring your own provider” motion (https://celchat.com/).

Buyers and triggers
Head of CX, contact-centre manager, Head of Support (SoW). Triggers: missed SLAs, Instagram / WhatsApp / web chat in three inboxes, collision (two agents reply at once), no shared history, expensive or rigid current inbox, hiring “WhatsApp support” or “omnichannel CX” roles, negative reviews of the current inbox tool.

India vs global
Abroad first, as Lalit confirmed. Sequence: UK, then UAE/GCC, then a careful US motion, then SEA. India support teams can be a later cross-sell (Celetel customers who need an inbox).

Where they hang out

  • Customer Support Leaders — curated Slack for people who lead support/CX teams ($10/month after a free first month) plus a free Discord for practitioners: https://www.customersupportleaders.com/join
  • CX Accelerator Slack: https://www.cxaccelerator.com/community
  • Support Driven Slack (Hive Index, updated 8 Jun 2026, lists it at over 10,000 customer-service professionals): https://thehiveindex.com/topics/customer-service/ and https://www.linkedin.com/company/support-driven
  • r/CustomerService (Hive Index lists about 62,000 members): https://www.reddit.com/r/CustomerService/
  • G2 and Capterra category research (buyers comparing tools): G2’s WhatsApp marketing / inbox round-up includes Wati and respond.io (https://learn.g2.com/best-whatsapp-marketing-software); CPaaS comparison: https://learn.g2.com/best-cpaas-platforms; product pages https://www.g2.com/products/wati/reviews and https://www.g2.com/products/interakt/reviews; Capterra WATI: https://www.capterra.com/p/204314/WATI/
  • Twilio, Infobip, Vonage and Bird official docs, blogs and customer/community spaces — these are where their existing users already are, and CelChat is an inbox layer on top, not a rip-and-replace of the CPaaS.

How to find lists

  • Technographics: BuiltWith / Wappalyzer-class detection of Twilio, client-side messaging widgets, and Instagram/WhatsApp chat plugins; Apollo / LinkedIn Sales Navigator filters for titles (Head of CX, Support Manager, Contact Centre) in the UK, UAE and (narrowly) the US, plus keywords “Twilio” or “Infobip” in CVs or job posts.
  • Job posts: “Twilio”, “WhatsApp Business API”, “contact centre”, “omnichannel support” on LinkedIn Jobs and Indeed (UK/UAE/US).
  • G2/Capterra reviewers of respond.io, WATI, Trengo, Freshdesk, Zendesk messaging — these are people who have already evaluated inboxes.
  • Company career pages and LinkedIn Jobs for teams hiring multiple support agents (the SoW’s 5–200 range is a filter, not a proven average).

Core message / offer
Keep the CPaaS you already pay (Twilio / Infobip / Vonage / Bird). Put WhatsApp, Instagram, RCS and web chat into one CelChat inbox, with routing, SLA timers and collision detection. 14-day trial, no credit card (https://celchat.com/). For UK/UAE, lead with SLA and one-thread history, not with “cheap Indian WhatsApp rates.” For the US, lead with support/utility and diaspora or cross-border conversations; do not promise marketing template delivery to US numbers until Meta’s current rules are re-checked. Self-serve or recorded demos should be the default, given timezones (Lalit’s request, 18 Nov).

3) ICP H — Competitor switchers — third, but on the same lists as A and G

Who
Current users of WATI, Interakt, AiSensy, Gallabox, Gupshup, respond.io, Trengo and similar (SoW list). Buyer is whoever owns the tool (founder, growth, or CX).

Triggers
Pricing complaints, support complaints, missing features (SoW). Public review sites and “WATI alternative” / “Interakt pricing” style searches (already in the design doc’s keyword set).

Geos
Same as A (India) and G (UK/UAE/US). Indian SMB WhatsApp-cloud tools (WATI, Interakt, AiSensy, Gallabox) are the natural Celetel+CelChat switch. Global inboxes (respond.io, Trengo) are the natural CelChat switch, keeping the existing BSP.

Where they hang out / how to find them
G2 and Capterra comparison pages and 1-star/2-star reviews; Shopify App Store reviews of the apps above; BuiltWith-style widget detection; X and LinkedIn keyword listening (the design doc already lists “wati alternative”, “interakt pricing”, “aisensy”, “gupshup down”).

Core message / offer (draft — needs Lalit’s yes)
Lalit said only “Can plan.” Recommended offer to approve, not to send yet: a free template-and-number migration, a written cost comparison, and a 14-day trial on the equivalent Celetel or CelChat plan. No public disparagement of named competitors in ads; keep the comparison factual and use a comparison page once proof numbers are approved.

4) ICP C — Real estate (India)

Who
Developers launching projects, and large brokerages (SoW). Buyers: sales and marketing heads. Pains: lead response speed, site-visit no-shows — also the use case already shown on celetel.com (“automate property inquiries, schedule site visits, share brochures via RCS”).

Geos
Same first metros (Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru), then other high-activity RERA markets. Do not invent city-level developer counts. The design doc already names MahaRERA, K-RERA and HRERA as scraper sources for new project registrations — use official RERA lists, not scraped personal phone books.

Where they hang out / how to find them
Google Maps categories (real-estate agents, property developers, “housing project”); official RERA registrant lists; LinkedIn titles (VP Sales, GM Marketing at developers); Instagram/Facebook Click-to-WhatsApp ads for projects; local developer summits (only add a named event once we have a current URL and date). Capacity-style telecom events are more relevant to partners than to brokers.

Message
Every property enquiry gets a WhatsApp or RCS reply in minutes, a brochure, and a booked site visit, without the sales team living in a shared WhatsApp phone. AI Agents for after-hours qualification, handoff to a human for the visit.

5) ICP I — Channel partners

Who
Digital agencies, Shopify agencies, Zoho/HubSpot partners, CRM consultants (SoW). Buyer: agency founder. Offer: a white-label or referral line on Celetel (white label is “talk to sales” on https://www.celetel.com/pricing — confirm partner terms with Lalit before promising them).

Geos
Same Indian metros as ICP A, because that is where the Shopify/D2C agency density will follow the stores. UK agencies only after the UK CelChat motion has a partner one-pager.

Where they hang out / how to find them
ShopBrew’s agency dinners and Shopify meetups (https://shopbrew.co/); Shopify Partner Directory; Zoho and HubSpot partner directories; LinkedIn titles (“Shopify expert”, “HubSpot partner”); eTailVerse and D2C Insider enabler tracks.

Message
Add WhatsApp/RCS/SMS as a recurring revenue line. You keep the client relationship; Celetel is the rail. Confirm commission or white-label terms before this sequence goes live.

6) ICP D — Healthcare (India)

Who
Diagnostic chains, hospital groups, clinic chains (SoW). Buyers: operations head, COO. Pains: appointment no-shows, report delivery (SoW and Celetel’s own healthcare use-case copy).

Geos
Delhi NCR, Mumbai and Bengaluru first — these are where large accredited chains publicly operate campuses (for example Apollo lists NABH/NABL facilities in Noida, Bengaluru, Navi Mumbai and New Delhi: https://www.apollohospitals.com/accreditations). Do not invent bed counts or “number of hospitals in Bangalore.”

Where they hang out / how to find them
Google Maps (hospitals, diagnostic labs, clinics); hospital group websites and accreditation lists; healthcare operations LinkedIn titles; later, a named healthcare IT or hospital-leaders event only once a current edition is confirmed.

Message
WhatsApp/RCS appointment reminders and report alerts, with DLT SMS fallback. Stress delivery reliability and compliance; do not use unverified scale claims. Case studies are a blocker for many of these buyers — park large chains until Lalit can introduce or approve a story.

7) ICP E — EdTech & coaching (India)

Who
EdTech companies, coaching institutes, universities (SoW). Buyers: admissions and marketing heads. Pains: admission-season lead handling, fee reminders.

Geos
The same metros, plus well-known coaching cities that already appear in public D2C/store data (for example Jaipur ranks high in Merchant Data’s city table). Use Google Maps “coaching institute”, “university”, “test preparation” rather than inventing a city rank for coaching.

Where they hang out / how to find them
Google Maps; institute websites; LinkedIn admissions/marketing titles; Instagram “DM for admission” behaviour (route to email/LinkedIn outreach, not unsolicited WhatsApp blasts — per the design doc’s compliance rules).

Message
Reply to every admission enquiry on WhatsApp in minutes; automatic fee reminders; one inbox in exam season when volume spikes.

8) ICP B — BFSI & fintech (India) — after proof exists

Who
NBFCs, lending apps, insurers, brokers, payment companies (SoW). Buyers: CTO, Head of Digital, Product head. Pains: OTP failures, EMI reminders, KYC, fraud alerts.

Geos
Mumbai (India’s financial centre), Delhi NCR and Bengaluru first. No headcount figures invented.

Where they hang out / how to find them
Global Fintech Fest in Mumbai is a recurring flagship (2026 edition was 8–11 September: https://www.globalfintechfest.com/). India Mobile Congress in New Delhi is a recurring telecom/tech flagship (2026 edition was 7–10 October: https://www.indiamobilecongress.com/). These are useful for 2027 planning and for exhibitor lists already published. LinkedIn titles in banking/NBFC digital teams; TRAI DLT registrant lists for businesses already sending SMS.

Message
Wait for approved proof numbers and at least one permissioned case study. Until then, do not run a volume BFSI sequence. If a warm intro appears, pitch OTP reliability, DLT compliance and documented delivery — not slogans.

9) ICP F — Logistics & travel

Who
3PLs, couriers, travel agencies, OTAs (SoW). Buyers: ops and CX heads. Pains: “where is my order” tickets, booking confirmations. UAE travel is a secondary international angle (see geos).

How to find them
Google Maps (courier, travel agency, logistics); DGCA / tourism licensee lists where public; career pages hiring “customer support – tracking”; Instagram/WhatsApp “book now” agencies in UAE (CelChat, bilingual templates).

Message
Proactive WhatsApp/RCS tracking and booking updates, with the reply landing in one inbox. Park as a volume motion until A and G are live.

5. Messages we will and will not use

Will use, once Lalit approves this doc

  • Celetel, India D2C: cart recovery, COD confirmation, order alerts, Click-to-WhatsApp ads that actually get answered; transparent published pricing; official WhatsApp API setup.
  • CelChat, global support teams: one inbox on top of the CPaaS you already have; SLAs, routing, collision detection; 14-day trial; self-serve or recorded demo.
  • Switch variant (only after a written “yes” on the offer): free migration of templates / numbers, cost comparison, trial.

Will not use until approved

  • Any website scale claim (“5,000+ businesses / 10M+ messages a day”, “300+ active clients / 120M+ messages daily”, CelChat’s “500+ organisations / 12k+ agents / 98M+ messages”). Lalit said the first two sets are wrong and asked for realistic numbers (tracker, 18 Nov 2026, 6:18 PM IST).
  • Named customer logos or stories, until permission exists (Lalit: “we can gather that and it may take some time”).
  • A free migration promise in emails or ads, until Lalit approves the offer.
  • US marketing-template campaigns.

Brand voice, from the design doc (still the working brief): Celetel — confident, reliable, numbers-driven, India-proud, but only with approved numbers. CelChat — friendly, modern, CX-team empathy. Founder — personal, opinionated, builder.

6. Still needed from Lalit to make this final

  1. Approval of this priority order and of the UK → UAE/GCC → careful US sequence.
  2. Official LinkedIn, Instagram and X handles for both brands (kickoff Q5, still unanswered).
  3. A realistic, approved proof-number set, plus any logos or stories we may use.

  5. A closed-won sheet (industry, size, city, product bought — anonymised is fine) and the sales team’s top objections, so the ₹1–100 Cr and 5–200 agent hypotheses can be replaced with real ranges.
  6. Who takes the 20 weekly demos, and whether we should build the self-serve demo first.
  7. Slack routing for interested replies (Lalit: “We use slack. can automate something up”).
  8. Partner / white-label commercial terms before ICP I outreach starts.
